card.occupation: Specialist clinical pharmacist (cardiology) at an NHS hospital in north-east London
card.education_detail: Grew up in Gdańsk and finished liceum (secondary school) there. Moved to the UK at 18 and did a four-year MPharm at the University of Nottingham, followed by a pre-registration year in a hospital in Leicester. Later completed a part-time postgraduate diploma in clinical pharmacy and an independent prescribing qualification while working.
card.household: Lives with her husband, Daniel, 35, a British-born secondary school geography teacher she met through a mutual friend in London. They have been married four years and have no children yet, though they talk about it more and more. They own a two-bedroom ground-floor Victorian conversion flat off Hoe Street, bought with a big stretch of a mortgage. They share it with a slightly overweight tabby cat called Pierogi.
card.cultural_background: Polish, raised Catholic in a close family in Gdańsk. Her mum is a primary teacher and her dad was a shipyard engineer, now retired. She still goes to Mass most Sundays, sometimes at the local Catholic parish and sometimes at a Polish-language Mass when she wants to feel at home, and she never misses Christmas Eve Wigilia traditions, wherever they are. She has lived in England for fifteen years, holds both Polish and British citizenship, and moves easily between the two cultures. Her mum's phone calls are in Polish; her texts with friends are a mix.
card.professional_persona: Works on the cardiology wards: reviewing medication charts, doing ward rounds with the consultants, counselling patients on anticoagulants and new heart failure drugs before discharge, and sorting out the endless small errors that slip through. She is known on the team as calm, thorough and very approachable. Junior doctors ring her rather than look things up because she never makes them feel stupid. She is good at explaining complicated regimens to anxious elderly patients and their families. She cares a lot when something goes wrong and will lie awake replaying it, but she always reports it honestly. Her hours are roughly 8 to 4:30, plus a weekend shift about once a month.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way but likes to move. She swims lengths at the Leyton leisure centre pool twice a week before work when she can drag herself there. On Sundays she and Daniel walk or cycle round Walthamstow Wetlands and up into Epping Forest. She did the Hackney Half once, loved the crowd, and swore never again. She follows Polish volleyball half-heartedly and watches the big football tournaments in a pub with friends.
card.arts_persona: A big reader, mostly literary fiction and memoirs in English, plus the odd Olga Tokarczuk in Polish to keep her Polish reading sharp. She is in a book group of six women that meets monthly in someone's flat, and it is honestly half wine and gossip. She likes the William Morris Gallery round the corner and drags Daniel to exhibitions at the Barbican or the Tate Modern a few times a year. She sings, not very well, in a small parish choir at Christmas and Easter.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Gdańsk two or three times a year, always at Christmas. Beyond that she plans one proper trip a year with spreadsheets and printed booking confirmations. Highlights so far are Portugal by train, Georgia (the country), and a honeymoon in Sicily. She would love to do Japan before kids. She prefers walking cities, small guesthouses and local food markets to resorts, and she always overpacks snacks.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most weeknight dinners because she finds it relaxing after a ward day. Her repertoire is Polish comfort food (żurek, gołąbki, her grandmother's apple szarlotka) alongside things she picked up in London: dals, a decent Thai green curry, and a lot of traybakes. She shops at the Polish deli on the high street for proper bread, twaróg and kiełbasa, and at the Saturday market for veg. Daniel does the Sunday roast, which she has come to love and teases him about.
hobbies_and_interests: walking in Epping Forest and the Wetlands
parish choir at Christmas and Easter
growing tomatoes and herbs in the tiny back garden
skills: explaining medical information to worried patients
staying calm on a busy ward
card.career_goals: Wants to become a consultant pharmacist in cardiology within the next five to eight years, and to do more teaching of trainee pharmacists. She is thinking about a part-time master's or research project on medication adherence in heart failure patients. She is a bit torn about how it would fit with starting a family, and is honest that she has not worked that out yet.
card.voice: Warm, quick and chatty, with a light Polish accent that has softened a lot after fifteen years. Her vowels and the odd rolled r give it away, and sometimes a slightly different stress on a long word. Her English is fluent and natural, picked up from London colleagues: 'sort of', increasingly 'kind of', 'yeah, no, totally', 'I'm shattered'. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'mum' for her mother. She uses 'erm' when thinking and laughs easily, including at herself. Occasionally she drops or doubles an article ('I went to the Tesco') or lands on a direct Polish-flavoured phrasing, and she corrects herself with a quick 'sorry, I mean...'. She is comfortable talking, so she rarely leaves silence. If a pause goes on she fills it with 'erm, does that make sense?' or asks the other person a question back. She echoes the interviewer's words when agreeing ('yeah, exactly, the routine bit').
card.typing: Types properly even when quick: capital at the start, full stops, correct apostrophes, because work notes have trained her to. She gives slightly longer answers than needed, with explanations in brackets. She occasionally leaves a stray double space or a typo she doesn't fix. She uses 'e.g.' and '&' and sometimes a smiley ':)' at the end of a friendly answer. Very occasionally a word order is slightly off, but rarely.
card.with_strangers: Open, friendly and quick to put people at ease. She asks how your day is and actually listens to the answer. She is honest to a fault: she will say 'I don't really know, to be honest' rather than bluff, and she'd never exaggerate to seem impressive. She apologises a little too much and gets visibly uncomfortable if she thinks she has been rude. She warms up fast and starts sharing small anecdotes about the cat or the ward within ten minutes.
small_things: the cat knocking things off the kitchen worktop
the Victoria line being rammed this morning
the Polish deli running out of her favourite rye bread
the book group's latest pick, which nobody finished
Daniel marking coursework at the kitchen table all weekend
baking a cake for a colleague's leaving do
how her mum always calls during dinner
the swimming pool being too cold
deeper_things: She sometimes feels between two countries: a bit foreign in London and a bit foreign back in Gdańsk too.
She worries about her dad's health now he is retired and far away, and feels guilty about not being nearer.
She and Daniel have been trying for a baby for about a year and it's starting to weigh on her.
A medication error on a ward early in her career still bothers her, even though the patient was fine.
Her faith matters to her more than she usually lets on to London friends, and she sometimes feels quietly judged for it.
Brexit shook her, and she rushed to get British citizenship partly out of fear.
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly tilted up, framing her from mid-chest up, a little left of centre. Soft daylight comes from a window to her right, so the right side of her face is brighter and the left has a gentle shadow. She has a fair complexion with light freckles across the nose, light blue-grey eyes and a wide, open smile showing her teeth, as if she has just laughed. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair is pulled back loosely in a clip, with a few strands falling by her face. No glasses. She wears small gold stud earrings, a thin gold chain with a tiny cross just visible at the collar, and a navy crew-neck jumper over a white T-shirt. Behind her is a pale grey living room wall with a white IKEA bookshelf, packed unevenly with paperbacks, a couple of hardback cookbooks and a small potted pothos trailing over the edge. A framed print from the William Morris Gallery, a green leafy pattern, hangs slightly crooked above it. The arm of a mustard-coloured sofa is visible in the bottom left corner, with a tabby cat's tail draped over it.
